title: feat: auth-flow drop-off tracking and signup funnel percentages
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Re-applies #14938 (reverted in #15025 before it reached production) together with its follow-ups, so the conversion tracking ships as one change. Addresses #14234.

**No browser identifier.** No cookie and no random id. The browser keeps only the referrer hostname and the campaign tags of the landing URL in `sessionStorage`, so they survive the GitHub redirect and a signed-in view still carries the source it came from. Attribution then joins on the server-authenticated `user_id`.

**Writes (all into Tinybird `product_event`, behind `TINYBIRD_ANALYTICS_ENABLED` / `VITE_TINYBIRD_ANALYTICS_ENABLED`)**
- Page views, signed in and signed out, via one same-origin beacon. Each carries page, referrer hostname, `utm_*` / `ref`, and the app key from the page URL. Values are length-capped, not filtered.
- Sign-in drop-off as two server-side counts: `sign_in_started` when GitHub is requested, `sign_in_completed` when the session exists. No browser state, so the `/app/sign-in` flow is covered too. Both honour DNT and Global Privacy Control.
- Device code issued / approved / denied / token, PKCE consent grants, Discord link start/complete, checkout started, auto top-up enabled/disabled with amount. No codes, tokens, emails or IPs. Rows expire after 24 months.

**Reads (pipes)**
- `traffic_sources`: source × campaign → views, users, signups, paid, by week.
- `kpi_signup_funnel`: registration week → Pollen/top-up view → checkout → paid, pct per stage.
- `auth_flow_funnel`: daily sign-in and device stages, pct per stage.
- `checkout_outcomes`: fulfilled vs expired vs failed Stripe sessions by pack, from existing `stripe_event`.
- `product_analytics_daily`: as in #14938, anonymous rows not counted as users.

**Tests**: analytics enabled in the test worker, `product_event` recorded by the Tinybird mock; beacon guards, attribution passthrough, sign-in start/complete through a real OAuth round trip, device approve/deny/token, PKCE consent, opt-out.

gist.headline: Following the pollen trail
gist.blurb: The hive can now see where a visit becomes a signup, checkout, or a politely abandoned GitHub redirect. It does this without cookies or a browser ID, because apparently software can remember less.
gist.summary: Added privacy-respecting Tinybird product analytics for page attribution, GitHub sign-in and device-code funnels, PKCE consent, Discord linking, checkout and auto-top-up events, plus weekly traffic-source and funnel-percentage pipes.
gist.impact: The team can measure signup, auth, and checkout stages—including drop-off percentages and campaign sources—using server-authenticated user IDs and session-only referrer/UTM data, with DNT and Global Privacy Control honored.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy observability garden: Polli follows a short trail of pollen dots from a landing-page flower through a GitHub-shaped sign-in gate to a blooming signup plant, while a friendly CRT robot reads a simple funnel chart. The trail represents session-only campaign/referrer attribution rather than cookies or persistent browser tracking; small privacy leaves and a DNT sign convey the opt-out safeguards.
